----- SECTION (2026-09-15, R-117 coordinate-canonicity gate on the EC value builtins) -----

R-117: a Point's WIDTH was gated by CL-BUG-095 (commit ea79620a); its two COORDINATES were never gated to be field elements. decomposePoint / cDecomposePoint BIN2NUM each half of the blob as an unsigned integer, so any width-fitting value is accepted -- x + p included, whenever x + p < 2^(8w). Field arithmetic downstream reduces mod p, so (x+p)||y behaves ARITHMETICALLY as the point (x, y), but affineAdd's two case selectors are bare OP_NUMEQUAL on the RAW decomposed values and do not reduce:  cond = (px == qx) AND (py == qy), notinf = NOT(px == qx AND NOT cond). For P and its alias both read 0, so the chord path runs on two equal points with den_chord = qx - px = 0 (mod p) and a Fermat inverse where inv(0) = 0.

----- SECTION (2026-09-15, R-156 ecMakePoint field-element gate) -----

R-156: `ecMakePoint(x, y)` was NOT INJECTIVE. Per coordinate it emitted `push 33, OP_NUM2BIN, push 32, OP_SPLIT, OP_DROP`. NUM2BIN(33) writes a 33-byte little-endian SIGN-MAGNITUDE script number, so byte 32 is exactly where the sign bit lives AND where any bits >= 2^256 land -- and the split drops precisely that byte.

REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION on @bsv/sdk's Spend, before the fix, with the secp256k1 point (1, 4218f20a...7e76a7ee):
    ecMakePoint( 1n, y)          -> 0000...0001 || 4218f20a...
    ecMakePoint(-1n, y)          -> the SAME bytes      (sign discarded)
    ecMakePoint(1n + 2^256, y)   -> the SAME bytes      (magnitude truncated)
    ecMakePoint( 1n, -y)         -> the SAME bytes      (and on the y half)
The y-half collision is the sharpest of the three: `ecMakePoint(x, 0n - y)` is how a contract author spells point negation by hand, and it silently produced (x, +y) -- the point being negated -- rather than (x, p-y) or an error.

THIS IS NOT COVERED BY R-117 and cannot be. The bytes ecMakePoint emits for -1n are the perfectly canonical encoding of 1, so the coordinate-canonicity gate on ecAdd / ecMul / ecNegate sees a well-formed Point and has nothing to reject. The aliasing happens before any Point exists. The two findings are independent, which is why they are separate commits.

----- SECTION (2026-09-15, R-157 ecMul on-curve-or-infinity gate) -----

R-157: the ladder's correctness argument holds only for points ON the curve, every tier wrote that down, and nothing enforced it.

`ecMul(P, k)` does not compute k*P. It computes ((k mod n) + 3n)*P: the MSB-first ladder adds 3n so that a fixed high bit is always set, and +3n is a NO-OP ONLY WHEN ord(P) DIVIDES n. Cofactor 1 gives ord(P) = n for every point on the curve, so the trick is sound there and nowhere else. A point off the curve lies on some other curve y^2 = x^3 + b' whose order is unrelated to n, and the whole computation silently answers a different question.

REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION on @bsv/sdk's Spend, before the fix, with the off-curve point P = (5, 7), which lies on y^2 = x^3 - 76:
    ecMul(P, 1n)  ->  c8b039d1...9438f2ff   which is NOT P
    ecMul(P, 2n)  ->  e673c72b...c8dde4c8   which is NOT 2P
Both match ((k mod n) + 3n)*P computed off-chain on that other curve EXACTLY, which is how the mechanism was identified rather than guessed. `ecMul(P, 1n) != P` is the whole finding: the primitive violated its own contract for every off-curve input, not merely a contrived one.

The degenerate sub-case is worse. For a 2-torsion point of the other curve -- any (x, 0) -- every multiple collapses to the all-zero blob, measured for k = 1, 2, 3, 5, because the ladder's unguarded mixed-add hits H = R = 0 mid-ladder, sets Z3 = 0, and a Jacobian accumulator at infinity can never leave it. Combined with R-053 -- which correctly taught ecAdd that the all-zero blob is the identity -- that turns a Schnorr-shaped s*G == R + e*P verifier into a free pass: choose an off-curve P of order 2, e*P is O, R + O is R, and any s with R = s*G verifies with no knowledge of any discrete log. R-053 is right and is not being undone; this is the other half of the same seam.

WHY THE NEW SIZE IS CORRECT. The emitted sqrt was wrong, not merely large. lowerSqrt emitted 16 unconditional Newton rounds seeded at guess = n with NO convergence test. ----- SECTION (2026-09-15, R-157 ecMul on-curve-or-infinity gate) -----

R-157: the ladder's correctness argument holds only for points ON the curve, every tier wrote that down, and nothing enforced it.

`ecMul(P, k)` does not compute k*P. It computes ((k mod n) + 3n)*P: the MSB-first ladder adds 3n so that a fixed high bit is always set, and +3n is a NO-OP ONLY WHEN ord(P) DIVIDES n. Cofactor 1 gives ord(P) = n for every point on the curve, so the trick is sound there and nowhere else. A point off the curve lies on some other curve y^2 = x^3 + b' whose order is unrelated to n, and the whole computation silently answers a different question.

REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION on @bsv/sdk's Spend, before the fix, with the off-curve point P = (5, 7), which lies on y^2 = x^3 - 76:
    ecMul(P, 1n)  ->  c8b039d1...9438f2ff   which is NOT P
    ecMul(P, 2n)  ->  e673c72b...c8dde4c8   which is NOT 2P
Both match ((k mod n) + 3n)*P computed off-chain on that other curve EXACTLY, which is how the mechanism was identified rather than guessed. `ecMul(P, 1n) != P` is the whole finding: the primitive violated its own contract for every off-curve input, not merely a contrived one.

The degenerate sub-case is worse. For a 2-torsion point of the other curve -- any (x, 0) -- every multiple collapses to the all-zero blob, measured for k = 1, 2, 3, 5, because the ladder's unguarded mixed-add hits H = R = 0 mid-ladder, sets Z3 = 0, and a Jacobian accumulator at infinity can never leave it. Combined with R-053 -- which correctly taught ecAdd that the all-zero blob is the identity -- that turns a Schnorr-shaped s*G == R + e*P verifier into a free pass: choose an off-curve P of order 2, e*P is O, R + O is R, and any s with R = s*G verifies with no knowledge of any discrete log. R-053 is right and is not being undone; this is the other half of the same seam.

WHY THE GATE BELONGS IN ecMul AND NOT IN THE CALLER. The +3n offset is INTERNAL to ecMul: a caller cannot see it, cannot know the obligation exists without reading the codegen, and gains nothing by checking what ecMul can check more cheaply (ecOnCurve is 816 bytes against ecMul's 428,754 -- 0.19%). The obligation WAS written down, in all seven tiers, in buildJacobianAddOrDoubleInline's own docstring: "callers who accept untrusted points must gate them on ecOnCurve first". Nothing enforced it, and the repository's own schnorr-zkp fixture takes its pubKey from a DEPLOYER-supplied constructor slot, where that idiom is not even reachable.

WHY NOT ecAdd, which is the other half of the boundary: affineAdd implements the group law with no n-dependent trick, so on an off-curve operand it returns the CORRECT sum on that operand's own curve -- it does not lie. And O, which is deliberately not on the curve, must keep flowing through ecAdd for R-053 to hold. Gating the adder would break a working primitive to fix a different one.

O IS EXEMPTED and the exemption is load-bearing: ecMul(P, 0n) returns the all-zero blob, ecAdd(P, -P) returns it, and the EC optimizer folds to it, so O is a reachable runtime operand -- while ecOnCurve(O) is false by construction (0^2 != 0^3 + b). A bare on-curve gate would reject the identity this codegen manufactures itself. The gate is therefore `onCurve(P) OR P == O`.

WHY THE NEW SIZE IS CORRECT. R-169 as filed covered pow AND sqrt; commit a3c4c0af fixed sqrt and changed zero lines mentioning pow. lowerPow unrolled exactly 32 conditional multiplies with NO guard on the exponent, so it computed base^min(exp, 32) and returned that CLAMPED value with no error for any larger exponent -- measured on @bsv/sdk Spend: pow(2,33) = 4294967296, pow(2,40) = 4294967296, pow(3,50) = 1853020188851841 (= 3^32), pow(2,-1) = 1. The constant folder computed the TRUE power for 0 <= exp <= 256 and the reference interpreter is exact for every exp >= 0, so inside the window 33 <= exp <= 256 the same source compiled fold-ON and fold-OFF produced scripts accepting MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE inputs.

The fix mirrors what sqrt got twenty lines away in the same files: the domain is ENFORCED rather than documented. lowerPow now emits, once per callsite, on the exponent:

    OP_DUP <0> <33> OP_WITHIN OP_VERIFY

= OP_DUP(1) + OP_0(1) + push 33 as 0x01 0x21(2) + OP_WITHIN(1) + OP_VERIFY(1) = 6 bytes. The constant folder's bound goes 256 -> 32 and the reference interpreter throws above 32, so all three implementations now refuse on exactly the same boundary.

The bound stays 32 rather than rising to the folder's old 256. That is a measured decision, not an omission: each extra unrolled round costs 8-9 script bytes AT EVERY CALLSITE (~2 KB to reach 256), and a raised bound would STILL need a guard at the new limit -- it moves the cliff rather than removing it.

R-117: a Point's WIDTH was gated by CL-BUG-095 (commit ea79620a); its two COORDINATES were never gated to be field elements. decomposePoint / cDecomposePoint BIN2NUM each half of the blob as an unsigned integer, so any width-fitting value is accepted -- x + p included, whenever x + p < 2^(8w). Field arithmetic downstream reduces mod p, so (x+p)||y behaves ARITHMETICALLY as the point (x, y), but affineAdd's two case selectors are bare OP_NUMEQUAL on the RAW decomposed values and do not reduce:  cond = (px == qx) AND (py == qy), notinf = NOT(px == qx AND NOT cond). For P and its alias both read 0, so the chord path runs on two equal points with den_chord = qx - px = 0 (mod p) and a Fermat inverse where inv(0) = 0.

REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION on @bsv/sdk's Spend with real secp256k1, before the fix, using the smallest-x secp256k1 point P = (1, 4218f20a...7e76a7ee) and P' = (1 + p, same y):
    ecAdd(P, P)   -> c7ffffff...4bb00d333   the correct 2P
    ecAdd(P, P')  -> fffffffe...81895441    x = p-2, i.e. -2x, and OFF CURVE
A script that SUCCEEDED and returned a blob that is not a point, for an input that denotes P + P. Both the R-052 doubling fix and the R-053 P + (-P) fix are driven by these same two selectors, so both are defeated by the same trick. The same reproduction runs on P-256 (x = 5) and P-384 (x = 2), where x + p likewise fits in the coordinate width.

THE FIX REJECTS RATHER THAN REDUCES. ecOnCurve / pNNNOnCurve already answer "no" to a non-canonical encoding (GAP-301 and its a = -3 twin), so reducing would leave the predicate and the value builtins disagreeing about whether the blob is a point at all. Rejecting keeps them aligned, and it is the policy CL-BUG-095 already set for the width: predicates clamp and flag, value producers OP_VERIFY. The gate is placed on the USER-FACING value builtins (ecAdd, ecMul, ecNegate and their P-256/P-384 twins) and deliberately NOT inside the shared decompose helper, because that helper is also on cEmitVerifyECDSA's path, where decompressPubKey and cEmitSigRangeGate have already decided -- with reasons recorded in their own docstrings -- that attacker-chosen bytes must make a total boolean builtin return false rather than abort the script. That placement is measurable, not asserted: p256-wallet, p384-wallet and r1-k1-wallet, which use only verifyECDSA_*, are byte-unchanged by this commit, while the ten-fixture EC sweep of R-052/R-053 moved them.

----- SECTION (2026-09-15, R-157 ecMul on-curve-or-infinity gate) -----

R-157: the ladder's correctness argument holds only for points ON the curve, every tier wrote that down, and nothing enforced it.

`ecMul(P, k)` does not compute k*P. It computes ((k mod n) + 3n)*P: the MSB-first ladder adds 3n so that a fixed high bit is always set, and +3n is a NO-OP ONLY WHEN ord(P) DIVIDES n. Cofactor 1 gives ord(P) = n for every point on the curve, so the trick is sound there and nowhere else. A point off the curve lies on some other curve y^2 = x^3 + b' whose order is unrelated to n, and the whole computation silently answers a different question.

REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION on @bsv/sdk's Spend, before the fix, with the off-curve point P = (5, 7), which lies on y^2 = x^3 - 76:
    ecMul(P, 1n)  ->  c8b039d1...9438f2ff   which is NOT P
    ecMul(P, 2n)  ->  e673c72b...c8dde4c8   which is NOT 2P
Both match ((k mod n) + 3n)*P computed off-chain on that other curve EXACTLY, which is how the mechanism was identified rather than guessed. `ecMul(P, 1n) != P` is the whole finding: the primitive violated its own contract for every off-curve input, not merely a contrived one.

The degenerate sub-case is worse. For a 2-torsion point of the other curve -- any (x, 0) -- every multiple collapses to the all-zero blob, measured for k = 1, 2, 3, 5, because the ladder's unguarded mixed-add hits H = R = 0 mid-ladder, sets Z3 = 0, and a Jacobian accumulator at infinity can never leave it. Combined with R-053 -- which correctly taught ecAdd that the all-zero blob is the identity -- that turns a Schnorr-shaped s*G == R + e*P verifier into a free pass: choose an off-curve P of order 2, e*P is O, R + O is R, and any s with R = s*G verifies with no knowledge of any discrete log. R-053 is right and is not being undone; this is the other half of the same seam.

WHY THE GATE BELONGS IN ecMul AND NOT IN THE CALLER. The +3n offset is INTERNAL to ecMul: a caller cannot see it, cannot know the obligation exists without reading the codegen, and gains nothing by checking what ecMul can check more cheaply (ecOnCurve is 816 bytes against ecMul's 428,754 -- 0.19%). The obligation WAS written down, in all seven tiers, in buildJacobianAddOrDoubleInline's own docstring: "callers who accept untrusted points must gate them on ecOnCurve first". Nothing enforced it, and the repository's own schnorr-zkp fixture takes its pubKey from a DEPLOYER-supplied constructor slot, where that idiom is not even reachable.

WHY NOT ecAdd, which is the other half of the boundary: affineAdd implements the group law with no n-dependent trick, so on an off-curve operand it returns the CORRECT sum on that operand's own curve -- it does not lie. And O, which is deliberately not on the curve, must keep flowing through ecAdd for R-053 to hold. Gating the adder would break a working primitive to fix a different one.

O IS EXEMPTED and the exemption is load-bearing: ecMul(P, 0n) returns the all-zero blob, ecAdd(P, -P) returns it, and the EC optimizer folds to it, so O is a reachable runtime operand -- while ecOnCurve(O) is false by construction (0^2 != 0^3 + b). A bare on-curve gate would reject the identity this codegen manufactures itself. The gate is therefore `onCurve(P) OR P == O`.

INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE FOR THE NEW BYTES:
  (1) packages/runar-testing/src/__tests__/r157-ecmul-curve-gate.test.ts executes every claim on @bsv/sdk's Spend across all three curves -- 28 assertions, 7 RED before the fix and GREEN after. Controls with teeth, all of which must stay green and would redden on an over-strict gate: mul(G, k) still works and lands on the curve; mul(G, 1) is G; mulGen(k) agrees with mul(G, k); mul(O, k) is still O for every k WHILE ecOnCurve(O) is false, which is exactly why a bare on-curve gate would not do; mul(P, 0n) still produces O; and ecAdd(G, O) = G, the deliberately-ungated half of the boundary.
  (2) Every tier was falsified individually: neutering the gate in one tier and rebuilding that tier's binary makes it, and only it, the lone outlier against the other six on ec-unit. Seven for seven.
  (3) All seven independently written compilers produce these exact bytes. Before regeneration the conformance run reported 0 IR/script mismatches BETWEEN compilers and 49 golden mismatches = 7 fixtures x 7 tiers, unanimous.
  (4) An exhaustive sweep of all 78 fixtures -- compiled, not grepped -- shows exactly 7 move and 71 byte-unchanged. p256-wallet, p384-wallet and r1-k1-wallet are again byte-unchanged, which is the measured confirmation that the gate is on the PUBLIC pNNNMul builtins and not inside the ladder shared with verifyECDSA -- where decompressPubKey and the signature range gate have already decided that attacker-chosen bytes must yield `false` from a total boolean builtin rather than abort. expected-ir.json does not move.
  (5) conformance/witnesses/real-crypto-execution.test.ts re-executes the moved fixtures' spends through a second engine and is green.

----- SECTION (2026-09-15, R-117 coordinate-canonicity gate on the EC value builtins) -----

R-117: a Point's WIDTH was gated by CL-BUG-095 (commit ea79620a); its two COORDINATES were never gated to be field elements. decomposePoint / cDecomposePoint BIN2NUM each half of the blob as an unsigned integer, so any width-fitting value is accepted -- x + p included, whenever x + p < 2^(8w). Field arithmetic downstream reduces mod p, so (x+p)||y behaves ARITHMETICALLY as the point (x, y), but affineAdd's two case selectors are bare OP_NUMEQUAL on the RAW decomposed values and do not reduce:  cond = (px == qx) AND (py == qy), notinf = NOT(px == qx AND NOT cond). For P and its alias both read 0, so the chord path runs on two equal points with den_chord = qx - px = 0 (mod p) and a Fermat inverse where inv(0) = 0.

REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION on @bsv/sdk's Spend with real secp256k1, before the fix, using the smallest-x secp256k1 point P = (1, 4218f20a...7e76a7ee) and P' = (1 + p, same y):
    ecAdd(P, P)   -> c7ffffff...4bb00d333   the correct 2P
    ecAdd(P, P')  -> fffffffe...81895441    x = p-2, i.e. -2x, and OFF CURVE
A script that SUCCEEDED and returned a blob that is not a point, for an input that denotes P + P. Both the R-052 doubling fix and the R-053 P + (-P) fix are driven by these same two selectors, so both are defeated by the same trick. The same reproduction runs on P-256 (x = 5) and P-384 (x = 2), where x + p likewise fits in the coordinate width.

THE FIX REJECTS RATHER THAN REDUCES. ecOnCurve / pNNNOnCurve already answer "no" to a non-canonical encoding (GAP-301 and its a = -3 twin), so reducing would leave the predicate and the value builtins disagreeing about whether the blob is a point at all. Rejecting keeps them aligned, and it is the policy CL-BUG-095 already set for the width: predicates clamp and flag, value producers OP_VERIFY. The gate is placed on the USER-FACING value builtins (ecAdd, ecMul, ecNegate and their P-256/P-384 twins) and deliberately NOT inside the shared decompose helper, because that helper is also on cEmitVerifyECDSA's path, where decompressPubKey and cEmitSigRangeGate have already decided -- with reasons recorded in their own docstrings -- that attacker-chosen bytes must make a total boolean builtin return false rather than abort the script. That placement is measurable, not asserted: p256-wallet, p384-wallet and r1-k1-wallet, which use only verifyECDSA_*, are byte-unchanged by this commit, while the ten-fixture EC sweep of R-052/R-053 moved them.

----- SECTION (2026-09-15, R-157 ecMul on-curve-or-infinity gate) -----

R-157: the ladder's correctness argument holds only for points ON the curve, every tier wrote that down, and nothing enforced it.

`ecMul(P, k)` does not compute k*P. It computes ((k mod n) + 3n)*P: the MSB-first ladder adds 3n so that a fixed high bit is always set, and +3n is a NO-OP ONLY WHEN ord(P) DIVIDES n. Cofactor 1 gives ord(P) = n for every point on the curve, so the trick is sound there and nowhere else. A point off the curve lies on some other curve y^2 = x^3 + b' whose order is unrelated to n, and the whole computation silently answers a different question.

REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION on @bsv/sdk's Spend, before the fix, with the off-curve point P = (5, 7), which lies on y^2 = x^3 - 76:
    ecMul(P, 1n)  ->  c8b039d1...9438f2ff   which is NOT P
    ecMul(P, 2n)  ->  e673c72b...c8dde4c8   which is NOT 2P
Both match ((k mod n) + 3n)*P computed off-chain on that other curve EXACTLY, which is how the mechanism was identified rather than guessed. `ecMul(P, 1n) != P` is the whole finding: the primitive violated its own contract for every off-curve input, not merely a contrived one.

The degenerate sub-case is worse. For a 2-torsion point of the other curve -- any (x, 0) -- every multiple collapses to the all-zero blob, measured for k = 1, 2, 3, 5, because the ladder's unguarded mixed-add hits H = R = 0 mid-ladder, sets Z3 = 0, and a Jacobian accumulator at infinity can never leave it. Combined with R-053 -- which correctly taught ecAdd that the all-zero blob is the identity -- that turns a Schnorr-shaped s*G == R + e*P verifier into a free pass: choose an off-curve P of order 2, e*P is O, R + O is R, and any s with R = s*G verifies with no knowledge of any discrete log. R-053 is right and is not being undone; this is the other half of the same seam.

WHY THE GATE BELONGS IN ecMul AND NOT IN THE CALLER. The +3n offset is INTERNAL to ecMul: a caller cannot see it, cannot know the obligation exists without reading the codegen, and gains nothing by checking what ecMul can check more cheaply (ecOnCurve is 816 bytes against ecMul's 428,754 -- 0.19%). The obligation WAS written down, in all seven tiers, in buildJacobianAddOrDoubleInline's own docstring: "callers who accept untrusted points must gate them on ecOnCurve first". Nothing enforced it, and the repository's own schnorr-zkp fixture takes its pubKey from a DEPLOYER-supplied constructor slot, where that idiom is not even reachable.

WHY NOT ecAdd, which is the other half of the boundary: affineAdd implements the group law with no n-dependent trick, so on an off-curve operand it returns the CORRECT sum on that operand's own curve -- it does not lie. And O, which is deliberately not on the curve, must keep flowing through ecAdd for R-053 to hold. Gating the adder would break a working primitive to fix a different one.

O IS EXEMPTED and the exemption is load-bearing: ecMul(P, 0n) returns the all-zero blob, ecAdd(P, -P) returns it, and the EC optimizer folds to it, so O is a reachable runtime operand -- while ecOnCurve(O) is false by construction (0^2 != 0^3 + b). A bare on-curve gate would reject the identity this codegen manufactures itself. The gate is therefore `onCurve(P) OR P == O`.

INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE FOR THE NEW BYTES:
  (1) packages/runar-testing/src/__tests__/r157-ecmul-curve-gate.test.ts executes every claim on @bsv/sdk's Spend across all three curves -- 28 assertions, 7 RED before the fix and GREEN after. Controls with teeth, all of which must stay green and would redden on an over-strict gate: mul(G, k) still works and lands on the curve; mul(G, 1) is G; mulGen(k) agrees with mul(G, k); mul(O, k) is still O for every k WHILE ecOnCurve(O) is false, which is exactly why a bare on-curve gate would not do; mul(P, 0n) still produces O; and ecAdd(G, O) = G, the deliberately-ungated half of the boundary.

  (3) All seven independently written compilers produce these exact bytes. Before regeneration the conformance run reported 0 IR/script mismatches BETWEEN compilers and 49 golden mismatches = 7 fixtures x 7 tiers, unanimous.
  (4) An exhaustive sweep of all 78 fixtures -- compiled, not grepped -- shows exactly 7 move and 71 byte-unchanged. p256-wallet, p384-wallet and r1-k1-wallet are again byte-unchanged, which is the measured confirmation that the gate is on the PUBLIC pNNNMul builtins and not inside the ladder shared with verifyECDSA -- where decompressPubKey and the signature range gate have already decided that attacker-chosen bytes must yield `false` from a total boolean builtin rather than abort. expected-ir.json does not move.
  (5) conformance/witnesses/real-crypto-execution.test.ts re-executes the moved fixtures' spends through a second engine and is green.

----- SECTION 1 (2026-09-01, gh:brendan-elas — Any-S OP_PUSH_TX preimage binding) -----

Regenerated for the Any-S OP_PUSH_TX preimage-binding construction: the fixed binding blob emitted into every covenant method shrinks from 760 to 428 bytes (k=1 with r=Gx eliminating the k-inverse multiply; signing key d = 2^248*Gx^-1 mod n so the r*d addend is built on-stack; split/cat reversals; DER s taken from its minimal script-number encoding; branchless mod-n/low-S). Every changed golden is a pure function of the blob bytes: the delta is the blob substring plus recomputed offsets/lengths derived from it. Intentional spec change, corroborated by independent oracles: (1) the BSV Spend interpreter e2e suite (packages/runar-testing oppushtx-binding.test.ts) verifies the new blob ACCEPTS the genuine tx sighash preimage and REJECTS forged/decoupled and zeroed preimages (the BUG-100 exploit), across a 60-context sighash sweep plus 4 ground DER/low-S edge contexts (both malleation branches, 31-byte and 30-byte s); (2) the derived-key math (pubkey 02b405d7... = (2^248*Gx^-1 mod n)*G) was re-derived off-chain from the curve parameters alone; (3) all seven independently written tiers (TS, Go, Rust, Python, Ruby, Java, Zig) regenerate byte-identical goldens — conformance 72/72, sdk-output 59 cases x 7 SDKs clean, sdk-vertical 39/39 x 7 tiers, analyzer 24 pass / 0 fail; (4) 269 Go integration tests and 229 TS integration tests pass against a live bitcoin-sv regtest node, spending real covenant outputs that carry the new blob.

----- SECTION 2 (2026-09-15, R-135 WOTS+ signature-length gate) -----

R-135: verifyWOTS shipped with NO signature-length gate. The emitted verifier consumes the signature 32 bytes at a time with OP_SPLIT, 67 times, then dropped whatever was left over — the TS emitter's own comment said "drop empty sigRest" without ever checking that it was empty. REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION before any byte was touched, not inferred from the opcodes: packages/runar-testing r135-wots-length-gate.test.ts runs the compiled locking script on @bsv/sdk's Spend interpreter, and a genuine 2144-byte WOTS+ signature with a single 0x00 appended returned success=true, as did the same signature with 4096 attacker-chosen 0xab bytes appended. The reference implementation in packages/runar-testing/src/crypto/wots.ts has always rejected a wrong-length signature (`if (sig.length !== LEN * N) return false`), so this was a live divergence between the two oracles, not a shared design decision. WHAT THE ATTACKER GAINED, measured rather than asserted: malleability and nothing more. The verdict is a pure function of the first 2144 bytes, so padding never rescued a tampered signature (tested: still false), never made a signature verify against a different message (still false), and prefixed junk still failed; short signatures already aborted inside OP_SPLIT. What it did buy is unbounded third-party rewriting of the unlocking script: any relaying node could append arbitrary bytes to the WOTS signature of an in-flight transaction, changing its txid without invalidating it — which breaks chains of unconfirmed spends and the pre-signed stateful continuations the stateful-wots-gate fixture exists to exercise — and inflate the transaction's size, and so lower its effective fee rate, without limit. THE FIX is a 5-byte prologue gate, OP_SIZE <2144> OP_EQUALVERIFY, emitted once per verifyWOTS at the point where the signature is already on top of the stack (net stack effect zero). 2144 = LEN(67) * N(32) is written in every tier as `67 * 32` from named WOTS+ parameters, not as a magic number; WOTS+ here has a single parameter set (w=16, n=32, len1=64, len2=3), so the bound is a constant and there is no parameter to track — unlike SLH-DSA, whose sibling BUG-011 guard derives its length per FIPS-205 parameter set. The gate follows that SLH-DSA prologue convention exactly (OP_SIZE / push / OP_EQUALVERIFY, hard failure rather than a false result), which is consistent with the primitive already aborting on a short signature. EVIDENCE FOR THE NEW BYTES, none of it self-graded: (1) the reproduction test is executed on the real Spend interpreter, and it carries two CONTROLS with teeth — a genuine correctly-sized signature must still verify, and a second real signature over a different message must still verify; setting the bound to 2145 instead of 2144 reddens BOTH controls (exit 1, 4 failures) while the attack cases flip, so an over-strict gate cannot hide here; (2) FALSIFIED per tier: deleting the three gate ops from exactly one of the seven emitters, rebuilding that tier's binary, and re-running conformance reddens exactly that tier and no other — 'majority [six tiers] vs [neutered tier] first differs at byte 13', seven times out of seven, each with a non-zero exit; (3) all seven independently written compilers regenerate these exact bytes byte-for-byte, with no cross-tier script or IR mismatch reported by the conformance runner; (4) an exhaustive sweep of all 78 conformance fixtures shows exactly 3 move and 75 are byte-unchanged, and every fixture grows by exactly +5 bytes — the gate's own width, once — which confirms the change is confined to the WOTS+ family and emits one gate per call; expected-ir.json is unchanged everywhere because the gate lives in stack lowering, below ANF.

SECTION 2 SCOPE: this fixture composes the SECTION 1 stateful covenant blob with a verifyWOTS call. R-135 adds 5 bytes inside the verifyWOTS body only; the binding blob SECTION 1 describes is byte-unchanged, and its evidence still stands for the parts of this script it covers.

The previous goldens were graded only against signatures this repo produced with the same buggy signer -- the BUG-101 self-consistency trap. Scripts shrank slightly (the PICKed key-pair address is cheaper than a 4-byte push); expected-ir.json did not move, because the change is confined to stack lowering. All 7 tiers emit byte-identical hex for this fixture (conformance 72/72 in both fold modes). This fixture is SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s (n=16, SHA-256-only per FIPS 205 Table 2) -- the EXACT parameter set the ACVP vector covers -- and it is verified END-TO-END THROUGH THE COMPILED SCRIPT, not merely through the off-chain helper, by packages/runar-testing/src/__tests__/post-quantum-slh-acvp-onchain.test.ts, which replays the NIST signature on @bsv/sdk's Spend interpreter and requires accept, plus reject on a 1-bit tamper. F-038 / R34 (user decision 2026-10-04): expected-ir.json gains one top-level key parentClass (value = the contract's base class, checked against TS parse for all 85 fixtures); dispatcher verified the diff is exactly +1 line and no expected-script.hex moved; all 7 tiers agree (golden 85/85, --ir-parity 85, --ir-roundtrip 85) || PREVIOUS: NEW-014: `&&` / `||` now SHORT-CIRCUIT on-chain. They lowered to OP_BOOLAND / OP_BOOLOR, which are binary stack ops -- both operands must already be ON the stack, so both were evaluated unconditionally. spec/semantics.md 3.7 licensed that with "This is safe in Runar because all expressions are pure (no side effects beyond assert)", but purity is not TOTALITY: 10 of the same document lists division by zero as a runtime failure, and OP_SPLIT / OP_NUM2BIN abort out of range. Evaluating the operand the source skipped therefore ABORTED the script, so the ordinary defensive guard `assert(d === 0n || (100n / d) > 1n)` compiled to a locking script the chain rejects for exactly the input the guard exists to protect -- a permanently unspendable UTXO -- while the AST interpreter (which short-circuits) reported success. `&&` / `||` now desugar to the ternary, which stack lowering already emits as real OP_IF / OP_ELSE control flow (3.9 already specified the untaken arm as unevaluated), so the moved bytes are OP_BOOLAND/OP_BOOLOR (0x9a/0x9b) becoming OP_IF/OP_ELSE/OP_ENDIF (0x63/0x67/0x68). EVIDENCE IS THE DIFFERENTIAL ORACLE, NOT A SELF-GOLDEN: the OLD bytes are REJECTED by @bsv/sdk's real Spend.validate() on inputs the source accepts. The three specific consensus rejections pinned in packages/runar-testing/src/__tests__/shortcircuit-consensus-vm.test.ts are "OP_DIV cannot divide by zero!" (d=0 through a `||` zero-guard), "OP_SPLIT requires the first stack item to be a non-negative number less than or equal to the size of the second-from-top stack item" (a guarded out-of-range substr), and "OP_NUM2BIN requires that the size expressed in the top stack item is large enough to hold the value expressed in the second-from-top stack item" (a guarded undersized num2bin). That suite pins BOTH directions for every short-circuiting case -- the input that must not reach the right operand, the input that must reach it and hold, and the input that must reach it and reject -- so a compiler that simply dropped the right operand could not pass it. All 7 tiers emit byte-identical hex and IR for this fixture in both fold modes (conformance 72/72), and the regeneration moved ONLY the six files of the three fixtures whose sources use `&&` / `||`; a control regeneration on the unpatched tree was a byte-for-byte no-op, so every moved byte is attributable to this change alone. THIS FILE: the ANF IR (the desugar happens in ANF lowering, so the IR moves too) for fixture `boolean-logic`, whose source examples/ts/boolean-logic/BooleanLogic.runar.ts uses both `&&` and `||`, including a nested `bothAbove || (eitherAbove && notFlag)`. Its bytes move because those operators change lowering; no other behaviour of the fixture changed.

----- SECTION (2026-09-15, R-157 ecMul on-curve-or-infinity gate) -----

R-157: the ladder's correctness argument holds only for points ON the curve, every tier wrote that down, and nothing enforced it.

`ecMul(P, k)` does not compute k*P. It computes ((k mod n) + 3n)*P: the MSB-first ladder adds 3n so that a fixed high bit is always set, and +3n is a NO-OP ONLY WHEN ord(P) DIVIDES n. Cofactor 1 gives ord(P) = n for every point on the curve, so the trick is sound there and nowhere else. A point off the curve lies on some other curve y^2 = x^3 + b' whose order is unrelated to n, and the whole computation silently answers a different question.

REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION on @bsv/sdk's Spend, before the fix, with the off-curve point P = (5, 7), which lies on y^2 = x^3 - 76:
    ecMul(P, 1n)  ->  c8b039d1...9438f2ff   which is NOT P
    ecMul(P, 2n)  ->  e673c72b...c8dde4c8   which is NOT 2P
Both match ((k mod n) + 3n)*P computed off-chain on that other curve EXACTLY, which is how the mechanism was identified rather than guessed. `ecMul(P, 1n) != P` is the whole finding: the primitive violated its own contract for every off-curve input, not merely a contrived one.

The degenerate sub-case is worse. For a 2-torsion point of the other curve -- any (x, 0) -- every multiple collapses to the all-zero blob, measured for k = 1, 2, 3, 5, because the ladder's unguarded mixed-add hits H = R = 0 mid-ladder, sets Z3 = 0, and a Jacobian accumulator at infinity can never leave it. Combined with R-053 -- which correctly taught ecAdd that the all-zero blob is the identity -- that turns a Schnorr-shaped s*G == R + e*P verifier into a free pass: choose an off-curve P of order 2, e*P is O, R + O is R, and any s with R = s*G verifies with no knowledge of any discrete log. R-053 is right and is not being undone; this is the other half of the same seam.

WHY THE GATE BELONGS IN ecMul AND NOT IN THE CALLER. The +3n offset is INTERNAL to ecMul: a caller cannot see it, cannot know the obligation exists without reading the codegen, and gains nothing by checking what ecMul can check more cheaply (ecOnCurve is 816 bytes against ecMul's 428,754 -- 0.19%). The obligation WAS written down, in all seven tiers, in buildJacobianAddOrDoubleInline's own docstring: "callers who accept untrusted points must gate them on ecOnCurve first". Nothing enforced it, and the repository's own schnorr-zkp fixture takes its pubKey from a DEPLOYER-supplied constructor slot, where that idiom is not even reachable.

WHY NOT ecAdd, which is the other half of the boundary: affineAdd implements the group law with no n-dependent trick, so on an off-curve operand it returns the CORRECT sum on that operand's own curve -- it does not lie. And O, which is deliberately not on the curve, must keep flowing through ecAdd for R-053 to hold. Gating the adder would break a working primitive to fix a different one.

O IS EXEMPTED and the exemption is load-bearing: ecMul(P, 0n) returns the all-zero blob, ecAdd(P, -P) returns it, and the EC optimizer folds to it, so O is a reachable runtime operand -- while ecOnCurve(O) is false by construction (0^2 != 0^3 + b). A bare on-curve gate would reject the identity this codegen manufactures itself. The gate is therefore `onCurve(P) OR P == O`.

----- SECTION (2026-09-15, R-117 coordinate-canonicity gate on the EC value builtins) -----

R-117: a Point's WIDTH was gated by CL-BUG-095 (commit ea79620a); its two COORDINATES were never gated to be field elements. decomposePoint / cDecomposePoint BIN2NUM each half of the blob as an unsigned integer, so any width-fitting value is accepted -- x + p included, whenever x + p < 2^(8w). Field arithmetic downstream reduces mod p, so (x+p)||y behaves ARITHMETICALLY as the point (x, y), but affineAdd's two case selectors are bare OP_NUMEQUAL on the RAW decomposed values and do not reduce:  cond = (px == qx) AND (py == qy), notinf = NOT(px == qx AND NOT cond). For P and its alias both read 0, so the chord path runs on two equal points with den_chord = qx - px = 0 (mod p) and a Fermat inverse where inv(0) = 0.

REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION on @bsv/sdk's Spend with real secp256k1, before the fix, using the smallest-x secp256k1 point P = (1, 4218f20a...7e76a7ee) and P' = (1 + p, same y):
    ecAdd(P, P)   -> c7ffffff...4bb00d333   the correct 2P
    ecAdd(P, P')  -> fffffffe...81895441    x = p-2, i.e. -2x, and OFF CURVE
A script that SUCCEEDED and returned a blob that is not a point, for an input that denotes P + P. Both the R-052 doubling fix and the R-053 P + (-P) fix are driven by these same two selectors, so both are defeated by the same trick. The same reproduction runs on P-256 (x = 5) and P-384 (x = 2), where x + p likewise fits in the coordinate width.

THE FIX REJECTS RATHER THAN REDUCES. ecOnCurve / pNNNOnCurve already answer "no" to a non-canonical encoding (GAP-301 and its a = -3 twin), so reducing would leave the predicate and the value builtins disagreeing about whether the blob is a point at all. Rejecting keeps them aligned, and it is the policy CL-BUG-095 already set for the width: predicates clamp and flag, value producers OP_VERIFY. The gate is placed on the USER-FACING value builtins (ecAdd, ecMul, ecNegate and their P-256/P-384 twins) and deliberately NOT inside the shared decompose helper, because that helper is also on cEmitVerifyECDSA's path, where decompressPubKey and cEmitSigRangeGate have already decided -- with reasons recorded in their own docstrings -- that attacker-chosen bytes must make a total boolean builtin return false rather than abort the script. That placement is measurable, not asserted: p256-wallet, p384-wallet and r1-k1-wallet, which use only verifyECDSA_*, are byte-unchanged by this commit, while the ten-fixture EC sweep of R-052/R-053 moved them.

The boundary is pinned exactly: a coordinate of p-1 is ACCEPTED and a coordinate of p is REJECTED, on both halves of the blob, so the gate cannot be "< p" in name and something rounder in fact.

----- SECTION (2026-09-15, R-156 ecMakePoint field-element gate) -----

R-156: `ecMakePoint(x, y)` was NOT INJECTIVE. Per coordinate it emitted `push 33, OP_NUM2BIN, push 32, OP_SPLIT, OP_DROP`. NUM2BIN(33) writes a 33-byte little-endian SIGN-MAGNITUDE script number, so byte 32 is exactly where the sign bit lives AND where any bits >= 2^256 land -- and the split drops precisely that byte.

REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION on @bsv/sdk's Spend, before the fix, with the secp256k1 point (1, 4218f20a...7e76a7ee):
    ecMakePoint( 1n, y)          -> 0000...0001 || 4218f20a...
    ecMakePoint(-1n, y)          -> the SAME bytes      (sign discarded)
    ecMakePoint(1n + 2^256, y)   -> the SAME bytes      (magnitude truncated)
    ecMakePoint( 1n, -y)         -> the SAME bytes      (and on the y half)
The y-half collision is the sharpest of the three: `ecMakePoint(x, 0n - y)` is how a contract author spells point negation by hand, and it silently produced (x, +y) -- the point being negated -- rather than (x, p-y) or an error.

THIS IS NOT COVERED BY R-117 and cannot be. The bytes ecMakePoint emits for -1n are the perfectly canonical encoding of 1, so the coordinate-canonicity gate on ecAdd / ecMul / ecNegate sees a well-formed Point and has nothing to reject. The aliasing happens before any Point exists. The two findings are independent, which is why they are separate commits.

THE FIX REJECTS: each coordinate must satisfy 0 <= v < p, checked with OP_WITHIN and OP_VERIFY -- the same half-open bound the `within` builtin exposes to authors, in one opcode. Reducing mod p was considered and rejected for the reason R-117 gives: ecOnCurve answers "no" to a coordinate outside [0, p), so reducing here would leave the constructor and the predicate disagreeing about what a point is. Rejecting also restores INJECTIVITY, which is the property the defect broke.

----- SECTION (2026-09-15, R-157 ecMul on-curve-or-infinity gate) -----

R-157: the ladder's correctness argument holds only for points ON the curve, every tier wrote that down, and nothing enforced it.

`ecMul(P, k)` does not compute k*P. It computes ((k mod n) + 3n)*P: the MSB-first ladder adds 3n so that a fixed high bit is always set, and +3n is a NO-OP ONLY WHEN ord(P) DIVIDES n. Cofactor 1 gives ord(P) = n for every point on the curve, so the trick is sound there and nowhere else. A point off the curve lies on some other curve y^2 = x^3 + b' whose order is unrelated to n, and the whole computation silently answers a different question.

REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION on @bsv/sdk's Spend, before the fix, with the off-curve point P = (5, 7), which lies on y^2 = x^3 - 76:
    ecMul(P, 1n)  ->  c8b039d1...9438f2ff   which is NOT P
    ecMul(P, 2n)  ->  e673c72b...c8dde4c8   which is NOT 2P
Both match ((k mod n) + 3n)*P computed off-chain on that other curve EXACTLY, which is how the mechanism was identified rather than guessed. `ecMul(P, 1n) != P` is the whole finding: the primitive violated its own contract for every off-curve input, not merely a contrived one.

The degenerate sub-case is worse. For a 2-torsion point of the other curve -- any (x, 0) -- every multiple collapses to the all-zero blob, measured for k = 1, 2, 3, 5, because the ladder's unguarded mixed-add hits H = R = 0 mid-ladder, sets Z3 = 0, and a Jacobian accumulator at infinity can never leave it. Combined with R-053 -- which correctly taught ecAdd that the all-zero blob is the identity -- that turns a Schnorr-shaped s*G == R + e*P verifier into a free pass: choose an off-curve P of order 2, e*P is O, R + O is R, and any s with R = s*G verifies with no knowledge of any discrete log. R-053 is right and is not being undone; this is the other half of the same seam.

WHY THE GATE BELONGS IN ecMul AND NOT IN THE CALLER. The +3n offset is INTERNAL to ecMul: a caller cannot see it, cannot know the obligation exists without reading the codegen, and gains nothing by checking what ecMul can check more cheaply (ecOnCurve is 816 bytes against ecMul's 428,754 -- 0.19%). The obligation WAS written down, in all seven tiers, in buildJacobianAddOrDoubleInline's own docstring: "callers who accept untrusted points must gate them on ecOnCurve first". Nothing enforced it, and the repository's own schnorr-zkp fixture takes its pubKey from a DEPLOYER-supplied constructor slot, where that idiom is not even reachable.

WHY NOT ecAdd, which is the other half of the boundary: affineAdd implements the group law with no n-dependent trick, so on an off-curve operand it returns the CORRECT sum on that operand's own curve -- it does not lie. And O, which is deliberately not on the curve, must keep flowing through ecAdd for R-053 to hold. Gating the adder would break a working primitive to fix a different one.

O IS EXEMPTED and the exemption is load-bearing: ecMul(P, 0n) returns the all-zero blob, ecAdd(P, -P) returns it, and the EC optimizer folds to it, so O is a reachable runtime operand -- while ecOnCurve(O) is false by construction (0^2 != 0^3 + b). A bare on-curve gate would reject the identity this codegen manufactures itself. The gate is therefore `onCurve(P) OR P == O`.

  (4) An exhaustive sweep of all 78 fixtures -- compiled, not grepped -- shows exactly 7 move and 71 byte-unchanged. p256-wallet, p384-wallet and r1-k1-wallet are again byte-unchanged, which is the measured confirmation that the gate is on the PUBLIC pNNNMul builtins and not inside the ladder shared with verifyECDSA -- where decompressPubKey and the signature range gate have already decided that attacker-chosen bytes must yield `false` from a total boolean builtin rather than abort. expected-ir.json does not move.

----- SECTION (2026-10-13, N-110 ecAdd aborts on a y = 0 doubling) -----

N-110 (user decision: fail on y = 0 in all 7 tiers): secp256k1 affineAdd took its tangent path for P == Q with py == 0, where the tangent 3x^2 / 2y has no denominator, and because fieldInv is Fermat (inv(0) = 0) the script SUCCEEDED and returned (p - 2x, 0). ----- SECTION (2026-09-15, R-156 ecMakePoint field-element gate) -----

R-156: `ecMakePoint(x, y)` was NOT INJECTIVE. Per coordinate it emitted `push 33, OP_NUM2BIN, push 32, OP_SPLIT, OP_DROP`. NUM2BIN(33) writes a 33-byte little-endian SIGN-MAGNITUDE script number, so byte 32 is exactly where the sign bit lives AND where any bits >= 2^256 land -- and the split drops precisely that byte.

REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION on @bsv/sdk's Spend, before the fix, with the secp256k1 point (1, 4218f20a...7e76a7ee):

    ecMakePoint(-1n, y)          -> the SAME bytes      (sign discarded)
    ecMakePoint(1n + 2^256, y)   -> the SAME bytes      (magnitude truncated)
    ecMakePoint( 1n, -y)         -> the SAME bytes      (and on the y half)
The y-half collision is the sharpest of the three: `ecMakePoint(x, 0n - y)` is how a contract author spells point negation by hand, and it silently produced (x, +y) -- the point being negated -- rather than (x, p-y) or an error.

THIS IS NOT COVERED BY R-117 and cannot be. The bytes ecMakePoint emits for -1n are the perfectly canonical encoding of 1, so the coordinate-canonicity gate on ecAdd / ecMul / ecNegate sees a well-formed Point and has nothing to reject. The aliasing happens before any Point exists. The two findings are independent, which is why they are separate commits.

----- SECTION (2026-09-15, R-157 ecMul on-curve-or-infinity gate) -----

R-157: the ladder's correctness argument holds only for points ON the curve, every tier wrote that down, and nothing enforced it.

`ecMul(P, k)` does not compute k*P. It computes ((k mod n) + 3n)*P: the MSB-first ladder adds 3n so that a fixed high bit is always set, and +3n is a NO-OP ONLY WHEN ord(P) DIVIDES n. Cofactor 1 gives ord(P) = n for every point on the curve, so the trick is sound there and nowhere else. A point off the curve lies on some other curve y^2 = x^3 + b' whose order is unrelated to n, and the whole computation silently answers a different question.

REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION on @bsv/sdk's Spend, before the fix, with the off-curve point P = (5, 7), which lies on y^2 = x^3 - 76:
    ecMul(P, 1n)  ->  c8b039d1...9438f2ff   which is NOT P
    ecMul(P, 2n)  ->  e673c72b...c8dde4c8   which is NOT 2P
Both match ((k mod n) + 3n)*P computed off-chain on that other curve EXACTLY, which is how the mechanism was identified rather than guessed. `ecMul(P, 1n) != P` is the whole finding: the primitive violated its own contract for every off-curve input, not merely a contrived one.

The degenerate sub-case is worse. For a 2-torsion point of the other curve -- any (x, 0) -- every multiple collapses to the all-zero blob, measured for k = 1, 2, 3, 5, because the ladder's unguarded mixed-add hits H = R = 0 mid-ladder, sets Z3 = 0, and a Jacobian accumulator at infinity can never leave it. Combined with R-053 -- which correctly taught ecAdd that the all-zero blob is the identity -- that turns a Schnorr-shaped s*G == R + e*P verifier into a free pass: choose an off-curve P of order 2, e*P is O, R + O is R, and any s with R = s*G verifies with no knowledge of any discrete log. R-053 is right and is not being undone; this is the other half of the same seam.

WHY THE GATE BELONGS IN ecMul AND NOT IN THE CALLER. The +3n offset is INTERNAL to ecMul: a caller cannot see it, cannot know the obligation exists without reading the codegen, and gains nothing by checking what ecMul can check more cheaply (ecOnCurve is 816 bytes against ecMul's 428,754 -- 0.19%). The obligation WAS written down, in all seven tiers, in buildJacobianAddOrDoubleInline's own docstring: "callers who accept untrusted points must gate them on ecOnCurve first". Nothing enforced it, and the repository's own schnorr-zkp fixture takes its pubKey from a DEPLOYER-supplied constructor slot, where that idiom is not even reachable.

WHY NOT ecAdd, which is the other half of the boundary: affineAdd implements the group law with no n-dependent trick, so on an off-curve operand it returns the CORRECT sum on that operand's own curve -- it does not lie. And O, which is deliberately not on the curve, must keep flowing through ecAdd for R-053 to hold. Gating the adder would break a working primitive to fix a different one.

O IS EXEMPTED and the exemption is load-bearing: ecMul(P, 0n) returns the all-zero blob, ecAdd(P, -P) returns it, and the EC optimizer folds to it, so O is a reachable runtime operand -- while ecOnCurve(O) is false by construction (0^2 != 0^3 + b). A bare on-curve gate would reject the identity this codegen manufactures itself. The gate is therefore `onCurve(P) OR P == O`.

R-117: a Point's WIDTH was gated by CL-BUG-095 (commit ea79620a); its two COORDINATES were never gated to be field elements. decomposePoint / cDecomposePoint BIN2NUM each half of the blob as an unsigned integer, so any width-fitting value is accepted -- x + p included, whenever x + p < 2^(8w). Field arithmetic downstream reduces mod p, so (x+p)||y behaves ARITHMETICALLY as the point (x, y), but affineAdd's two case selectors are bare OP_NUMEQUAL on the RAW decomposed values and do not reduce:  cond = (px == qx) AND (py == qy), notinf = NOT(px == qx AND NOT cond). For P and its alias both read 0, so the chord path runs on two equal points with den_chord = qx - px = 0 (mod p) and a Fermat inverse where inv(0) = 0.

REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION on @bsv/sdk's Spend with real secp256k1, before the fix, using the smallest-x secp256k1 point P = (1, 4218f20a...7e76a7ee) and P' = (1 + p, same y):
    ecAdd(P, P)   -> c7ffffff...4bb00d333   the correct 2P
    ecAdd(P, P')  -> fffffffe...81895441    x = p-2, i.e. -2x, and OFF CURVE
A script that SUCCEEDED and returned a blob that is not a point, for an input that denotes P + P. Both the R-052 doubling fix and the R-053 P + (-P) fix are driven by these same two selectors, so both are defeated by the same trick. The same reproduction runs on P-256 (x = 5) and P-384 (x = 2), where x + p likewise fits in the coordinate width.

THE FIX REJECTS RATHER THAN REDUCES. ecOnCurve / pNNNOnCurve already answer "no" to a non-canonical encoding (GAP-301 and its a = -3 twin), so reducing would leave the predicate and the value builtins disagreeing about whether the blob is a point at all. Rejecting keeps them aligned, and it is the policy CL-BUG-095 already set for the width: predicates clamp and flag, value producers OP_VERIFY. The gate is placed on the USER-FACING value builtins (ecAdd, ecMul, ecNegate and their P-256/P-384 twins) and deliberately NOT inside the shared decompose helper, because that helper is also on cEmitVerifyECDSA's path, where decompressPubKey and cEmitSigRangeGate have already decided -- with reasons recorded in their own docstrings -- that attacker-chosen bytes must make a total boolean builtin return false rather than abort the script. That placement is measurable, not asserted: p256-wallet, p384-wallet and r1-k1-wallet, which use only verifyECDSA_*, are byte-unchanged by this commit, while the ten-fixture EC sweep of R-052/R-053 moved them.

R-157: the ladder's correctness argument holds only for points ON the curve, every tier wrote that down, and nothing enforced it.

`ecMul(P, k)` does not compute k*P. It computes ((k mod n) + 3n)*P: the MSB-first ladder adds 3n so that a fixed high bit is always set, and +3n is a NO-OP ONLY WHEN ord(P) DIVIDES n. Cofactor 1 gives ord(P) = n for every point on the curve, so the trick is sound there and nowhere else. A point off the curve lies on some other curve y^2 = x^3 + b' whose order is unrelated to n, and the whole computation silently answers a different question.

    ecMul(P, 2n)  ->  e673c72b...c8dde4c8   which is NOT 2P
Both match ((k mod n) + 3n)*P computed off-chain on that other curve EXACTLY, which is how the mechanism was identified rather than guessed. `ecMul(P, 1n) != P` is the whole finding: the primitive violated its own contract for every off-curve input, not merely a contrived one.

The degenerate sub-case is worse. For a 2-torsion point of the other curve -- any (x, 0) -- every multiple collapses to the all-zero blob, measured for k = 1, 2, 3, 5, because the ladder's unguarded mixed-add hits H = R = 0 mid-ladder, sets Z3 = 0, and a Jacobian accumulator at infinity can never leave it. Combined with R-053 -- which correctly taught ecAdd that the all-zero blob is the identity -- that turns a Schnorr-shaped s*G == R + e*P verifier into a free pass: choose an off-curve P of order 2, e*P is O, R + O is R, and any s with R = s*G verifies with no knowledge of any discrete log. R-053 is right and is not being undone; this is the other half of the same seam.

The +3n offset is INTERNAL to ecMul: a caller cannot see it, cannot know the obligation exists without reading the codegen, and gains nothing by checking what ecMul can check more cheaply (ecOnCurve is 816 bytes against ecMul's 428,754 -- 0.19%). The obligation WAS written down, in all seven tiers, in buildJacobianAddOrDoubleInline's own docstring: "callers who accept untrusted points must gate them on ecOnCurve first". Nothing enforced it, and the repository's own schnorr-zkp fixture takes its pubKey from a DEPLOYER-supplied constructor slot, where that idiom is not even reachable.

WHY NOT ecAdd, which is the other half of the boundary: affineAdd implements the group law with no n-dependent trick, so on an off-curve operand it returns the CORRECT sum on that operand's own curve -- it does not lie. And O, which is deliberately not on the curve, must keep flowing through ecAdd for R-053 to hold. Gating the adder would break a working primitive to fix a different one.

O IS EXEMPTED and the exemption is load-bearing: ecMul(P, 0n) returns the all-zero blob, ecAdd(P, -P) returns it, and the EC optimizer folds to it, so O is a reachable runtime operand -- while ecOnCurve(O) is false by construction (0^2 != 0^3 + b). R-135: verifyWOTS shipped with NO signature-length gate. The emitted verifier consumes the signature 32 bytes at a time with OP_SPLIT, 67 times, then dropped whatever was left over — the TS emitter's own comment said "drop empty sigRest" without ever checking that it was empty. REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION before any byte was touched, not inferred from the opcodes: packages/runar-testing r135-wots-length-gate.test.ts runs the compiled locking script on @bsv/sdk's Spend interpreter, and a genuine 2144-byte WOTS+ signature with a single 0x00 appended returned success=true, as did the same signature with 4096 attacker-chosen 0xab bytes appended. The reference implementation in packages/runar-testing/src/crypto/wots.ts has always rejected a wrong-length signature (`if (sig.length !== LEN * N) return false`), so this was a live divergence between the two oracles, not a shared design decision. WHAT THE ATTACKER GAINED, measured rather than asserted: malleability and nothing more. The verdict is a pure function of the first 2144 bytes, so padding never rescued a tampered signature (tested: still false), never made a signature verify against a different message (still false), and prefixed junk still failed; short signatures already aborted inside OP_SPLIT. What it did buy is unbounded third-party rewriting of the unlocking script: any relaying node could append arbitrary bytes to the WOTS signature of an in-flight transaction, changing its txid without invalidating it — which breaks chains of unconfirmed spends and the pre-signed stateful continuations the stateful-wots-gate fixture exists to exercise — and inflate the transaction's size, and so lower its effective fee rate, without limit. THE FIX is a 5-byte prologue gate, OP_SIZE <2144> OP_EQUALVERIFY, emitted once per verifyWOTS at the point where the signature is already on top of the stack (net stack effect zero). 2144 = LEN(67) * N(32) is written in every tier as `67 * 32` from named WOTS+ parameters, not as a magic number; WOTS+ here has a single parameter set (w=16, n=32, len1=64, len2=3), so the bound is a constant and there is no parameter to track — unlike SLH-DSA, whose sibling BUG-011 guard derives its length per FIPS-205 parameter set. The gate follows that SLH-DSA prologue convention exactly (OP_SIZE / push / OP_EQUALVERIFY, hard failure rather than a false result), which is consistent with the primitive already aborting on a short signature. EVIDENCE FOR THE NEW BYTES, none of it self-graded: (1) the reproduction test is executed on the real Spend interpreter, and it carries two CONTROLS with teeth — a genuine correctly-sized signature must still verify, and a second real signature over a different message must still verify; setting the bound to 2145 instead of 2144 reddens BOTH controls (exit 1, 4 failures) while the attack cases flip, so an over-strict gate cannot hide here; (2) FALSIFIED per tier: deleting the three gate ops from exactly one of the seven emitters, rebuilding that tier's binary, and re-running conformance reddens exactly that tier and no other — 'majority [six tiers] vs [neutered tier] first differs at byte 13', seven times out of seven, each with a non-zero exit; (3) all seven independently written compilers regenerate these exact bytes byte-for-byte, with no cross-tier script or IR mismatch reported by the conformance runner; (4) an exhaustive sweep of all 78 conformance fixtures shows exactly 3 move and 75 are byte-unchanged, and every fixture grows by exactly +5 bytes — the gate's own width, once — which confirms the change is confined to the WOTS+ family and emits one gate per call; expected-ir.json is unchanged everywhere because the gate lives in stack lowering, below ANF.

At HEAD the same 42 mappings existed with identical opcodeIndex values and opcodes 2-8, 10-16, 18-24, 26-32, 34-39 on the loop header line instead, so the delta the pin authorizes vs the pre-fix output is exactly those 34 entries' line/column. Verified against: (1) the independent source-anchor oracle (conformance/source-map/run.ts checkSourceAnchors, which re-reads each claimed line/column from the real source file): byte-id/structural/anchor OK for bounded-loop in all 7 tiers; (2) a second (and third..seventh) implementation: all seven tiers produce the same opcodeIndex set and the same header/body/pre/post partition of it, opcode for opcode (each tier compiles its own surface, so absolute lines/columns differ by design), and each tier has its own red-then-green test asserting this map; (3) script hex unchanged (conformance golden STRICT and --multi-format bounded-loop in both fold modes), since source locations never reach the bytes.
